purpose: Define the minimum explicit integration required because Payload 3.87.1 native sessions do not satisfy the canonical Session contract by themselves.
nativeAuthority: Payload auth-enabled Users collection remains the native authentication/session authority for native fields and sid lifecycle until the integration boundary is executed and verified.
canonicalAuthority: The canonical ENT-SESSION contract remains the application-level semantic authority. No duplicate full session table is authorized by this contract.

integrationModel.principle: Extend or derive only the unsupported canonical dimensions; reuse Payload native session identity, createdAt and expiresAt where concrete runtime/schema evidence proves equivalence.
integrationModel.singleAuthority: A request must never be authorized by conflicting native-session and custom-session states.

canonicalMapping.id: Payload native session id (sid), subject to schema/runtime proof
canonicalMapping.createdAt: Payload native session createdAt, subject to schema/runtime proof
canonicalMapping.expiresAt: Payload native session expiresAt, subject to schema/runtime proof

login: derive and persist only a one-way refresh credential verifier/hash for the canonical integration state if refresh credential state is required
record canonical session linkage without creating a second session identity
validation: fail closed on disagreement between native and canonical state
logout: record durable canonical revocation state where required by the field contract
refresh: validate native session sid and canonical integration state
prevent reuse of a previously accepted refresh credential
atomically advance refresh state where the canonical contract requires rotation
ensure concurrent refresh has at most one successful successor
activity: update lastSeenAt only according to an explicit bounded runtime policy
never use lastSeenAt as the sole authorization decision

transactionRules: Native session creation and canonical integration state creation must have a deterministic ordering and compensating failure path.
Logout must not report success while required durable revocation state failed to persist.
Refresh rotation must use a compare-and-update or transactional equivalent so one predecessor cannot produce two valid successors.
Authorization checks must fail closed if native session state and canonical integration state cannot be reconciled.
Canonical integration state must reference the native sid rather than minting an independent session identifier.

migrationRules.forbidden: Do not create a complete second sessions table mirroring Payload sessions.
requiredEvidence: exact extension columns/storage selected for unsupported dimensions

securityRules: Refresh credential material must be one-way derived only and must never be returned, logged or placed in public DTOs/events.
Device identifiers must be privacy-safe and server-bound.
tokenVersion must be server-controlled and cannot be supplied by clients.
Revocation state must override stale caches and stale JWTs.
Canonical integration state cannot weaken Payload native session validation.
stopConditions: A second independent session identifier is introduced.
A full parallel sessions table is introduced without a revised contract.
Native sid can authorize after canonical revocation.
Refresh predecessor can be reused successfully after rotation.
Concurrent refresh can produce two valid successors.
Raw credential material is persisted or exposed.
Device binding is client-controlled or absent where required.
Any unsupported dimension is implemented without an explicit field mapping and migration evidence.
